dataset_family: Single-centre CSVD clinical cohort, First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China (MRI Oct 2023 - May 2024); not public
method_family: Multi-shell diffusion MRI with NODDI (FISO/NDI/ODI) in FreeSurfer hippocampal-subfield grey matter, compared with ICV-normalised subfield volume (grey-matter diffusion microstructure)
what_it_shows: Li B, Zeng B, ... Li Y (2025), J Affect Disord 384:12-22. 58 CSVD-MCI, 54 CSVD without cognitive impairment (NCI) and 57 HC, cross-sectional. Subfield volumes and NODDI metrics were compared by ANCOVA (age, education) with BH-FDR. FISO in left and right subiculum and CA1-3 was higher in CSVD-MCI than in CSVD-NCI and HC (left CA1-3 0.36 vs 0.32 vs 0.31, F 6.898, PFDR 0.005). Subfield volumes differed across groups, predominantly between the patient groups and HC. In the direct CSVD-MCI vs CSVD-NCI comparison, the authors report no significant hippocampal volume difference but significant left CA1-3 FISO and NDI differences; the pairwise statistics are in Supplementary Table 8, not the main text. NDI's omnibus test failed FDR (PFDR 0.066).
why: Identity: the PDF's title, authors (Li, Zeng ... Li Y; Chongqing) and DOI 10.1016/j.jad.2025.05.027 match the block and the map. I read the whole extract to the reference marker. Pages cited are PDF pages (journal pp. 12-20). STATED (Table A1) = partly. Part shown: within CSVD, a microstructural measure (FISO; NDI less securely) separates MCI from cognitively unimpaired CSVD where hippocampal volume does not. Not shown: (1) Volume is not preserved in this MCI group. Subfield volumes are reduced in both CSVD groups relative to HC, so volume does separate CSVD-MCI from HC; the regime is 'non-discriminative against a CSVD comparator', not 'preserved'. (2) 'Late' is an inference from a cross-sectional contrast, which is the authors' own stated limitation. (3) The population is vascular (CSVD) MCI with AD excluded, and nothing is tested on conversion. NARROWED = yes, scoped: in one small single-centre cohort, FISO carried information that hippocampal subfield volume did not for CSVD-MCI vs CSVD-NCI. The comparison is like-for-like (same subfield ROIs, same ANCOVA and FDR procedure). Caveats: (a) The pairwise MCI-vs-NCI volume and NDI statistics are in the supplement; the main text states the result in section 4.3 and gives the FISO three-group means in 3.2. (b) NDI's omnibus effect did not survive FDR, so FISO is the secure measure. (c) The authors flag possible CSF partial-volume contamination of FISO at 2 mm slices. (d) WMH Fazekas burden was higher in CSVD-MCI than in CSVD-NCI (p = 0.027), a possible confound for FISO. (e) Cross-sectional. Independence: the dataset is new (Chongqing), with no shared authors or site with any current supporter. The method family is diffusion MRI microstructure, the same broad family as P-581 (cortical minicolumn diffusivity, NACC) and candidate P-1425 (tract DTI). Whether hippocampal grey-matter NODDI counts as distinct from P-581's cortical diffusivity is an operator decision. Not a preprint. P-651 is also a VF-25 supporter, which does not affect VF-20 independence. In the quotes, soft hyphens, line-break hyphens and dashes are normalised to ASCII.

quotes.quote: Notably, FISO metrics demonstrated more pronounced differences during early cognitive decline stages compared to volumetric analyses.

The FISO indicator demonstrated the most pronounced group differences, with CSVD-MCI patients consistently showing significantly higher values compared to CSVD-NC and healthy controls, particularly in the left hemisphere subiculum (0.34 ± 0.11 vs. 0.30 ± 0.11 and 0.29 ± 0.08, F = 4.521, P = 0.012, PFDR = 0.028) and CA1-3 region (0.36 ± 0.10 vs. 0.32 ± 0.07 and 0.31 ± 0.06, F = 6.898, P = 0.001, PFDR = 0.005).
NDI measurements showed more limited variations, with only the left hemisphere CA1-3 region demonstrating marginally significant differences (F = 3.178, P = 0.044, PFDR = 0.066).

In the left hemisphere, subiculum showed significant group differences (F = 4.445, P = 0.013, PFDR = 0.02836), while CA1-3 and CA4-DG regions exhibited highly significant variations (CA1-3: F = 9.953, P < 0.001, PFDR = 0.00480; CA4-DG: F = 9.368, P < 0.001, PFDR = 0.00480). The right hemisphere mirrored these findings, with comparable significant differences observed across subiculum, CA1-3, and CA4-DG regions, predominantly between patient groups and healthy controls (Supplementary Material 2 Table 8).
When comparing the MCI with the NCI, we did not observe significant differences in hippocampal volume, but significant changes were found in the FISO and NDI metrics in the left CA1-3 region.

Particularly, since most of the hippocampus is surrounded by the lateral ventricles and cerebrospinal fluid, larger voxels inevitably contain some CSF signals, which may contaminate the measurement of microstructural parameters, especially affecting the FISO index.
First, the characteristics of the cross-sectional study design mean that the observed differences reflect group effects rather than individual dynamic changes during disease progression.
